title: Best Shopify QuickBooks Integration Solutions: 2026 Comparison
summary: Looking for the best Shopify QuickBooks integration? We compare top tools for 2026: features, pricing, and sync accuracy to help you decide.
body_markdown:
The best Shopify QuickBooks integration depends on your order volume, channel count, and QuickBooks version, because together they set how much data reaches your books. A solo store syncs one source, while a brand selling on Amazon, Faire, and wholesale has to merge several into one QuickBooks file.


Without an integration, that data is entered by hand: in demo calls with 412 retail merchants, 45.4% named manual data entry as their top accounting challenge. This guide reviews five tools so you can:


- Compare sync methods, pricing, volume limits, and QuickBooks Desktop support
- Match a tool to your business type
- Calculate cost per order at current and projected volume


With the right match, you can cut daily reconciliation[from 3-4 hours to under 45 minutes](https://synder.com/success-stories/healthy-meals-direct/) .


## **TL;DR**


1. Simple stores can start free: the native Intuit connector covers single-store sellers on QuickBooks Online.
2. Multi-channel sellers need a third-party tool that posts sales from multiple channels and processors to one QuickBooks file.
3. QuickBooks Desktop users have fewer options, so check Desktop support before anything else.
4. High-volume stores should use summary posting and compare cost per order, not monthly fees.
5. Accounting firms need separate client books, per-client rules, and partner pricing.


## **How automated QuickBooks Shopify sync cuts manual reporting**


Automated Shopify QuickBooks sync posts sales, refunds, fees, and payouts to QuickBooks as they happen, which removes the copy-and-paste step between the two systems. Without it, report creation starts with data consolidation: exporting Shopify orders, pulling processor statements, and rebuilding the same spreadsheet every month.


That manual layer is still common in finance teams in 2026. According to[Capterra’s 2026 Accounting Software Trends survey](https://www.capterra.com/resources/accounting-trends-ai-software-changing-work/) of 500 U.S. accounting decision-makers, 55% still handle financial reporting manually at least some of the time, and 51% keep part of their financial data in spreadsheets.


**With manual Shopify accounting, three complications keep the totals from matching:**


- **Batched payouts:** Shopify batches multiple days of sales into a single payout, so your $3,847 bank deposit doesn’t match any transaction in your books.
- **Multiple processors:** Shopify Payments handles some orders, PayPal processes others, and Stripe picks up the rest, each with different fee structures and payout schedules.
- **Jurisdiction-level sales tax:** Sales tax gets calculated by jurisdiction, but QuickBooks needs it broken down by state, county, and city.


One mistake means starting over, and by month-end, you’re buried in spreadsheets trying to piece together what actually happened.


[Automation](https://synder.com/blog/how-synder-sync-helps-e-commerce-brands/) lets you get rid of this. Special tools for integrating the platforms sync every transaction automatically. Sales, refunds, fees, taxes, and payouts go directly from Shopify to QuickBooks without manual data entry.


### **How payouts post when you sync Shopify with QuickBooks**


When you sync Shopify with QuickBooks, a payout posts as five elements, gross sales, sales tax, processing fees, refunds, and the net deposit, and they need separate accounts. The table below breaks down the $3,847 deposit from the example above.


**Element** **Example amount** **Where it posts in QuickBooks**


Gross sales $3,720 Income account


Sales tax collected $280 Sales tax liability mapping to Sales Tax Payable


Processing fees –$116 Fee expense account (processing fee allocation)


Refunds –$37 Refund journal entry that reduces sales


Net payout $3,847 Bank account, after bank deposit matching


#### **How a QuickBooks clearing account holds and checks Shopify payouts**


Integration tools post a payout’s sales, tax, fee, and refund lines to a QuickBooks clearing account first. The clearing account holds those lines until Shopify transfers the money. When the $3,847 deposit arrives, a transfer for that amount moves it to the bank account, and the clearing balance for that payout returns to zero.


Payout lines can be checked against the Shopify Payments payout report, which lists the orders, fees, and adjustments inside a deposit. If any line is missing, the clearing account shows a leftover balance for that payout date.


A clearing account also keeps the accrual vs cash basis accounting question clean: income is recorded on the order date, while the cash appears in the bank only when the payout settles.


### **Reporting and month-end close after you connect QuickBooks to Shopify**


Automated sync updates the P&L statement in QuickBooks as payouts post, so month-end reports start from categorized sales, fees, refunds, and taxes. You can filter revenue by channel, fees by processor, and refunds by period without building manual pivots. QuickBooks Custom Reports can pull those splits directly, as long as the integration maps sales, fees, refunds, and taxes to separate accounts or classes.


Business intelligence (BI) tools, such as Power BI or Tableau, build dashboards from the same accounting data. If you’re comparing which BI tools have the best built-in connectors for QuickBooks and Shopify, check whether they read from QuickBooks after sync or directly from Shopify and other platforms, because only the first uses reconciled numbers.


#### **Journal entry automation for summary posting**


Summary posting removes manual journal entries from the close. Journal entry automation creates one entry per payout or per day from the platform data, so nobody types it in from a statement.


Summary entries carry the payout date and reference, so you can trace them back to the processor. The bank reconciliation workflow in QuickBooks then compares one deposit with one bank line per payout.


#### **What month-end close automation delivers**


Accounting teams that automate close and reconciliation work report measurable returns. In the same Capterra survey, 89% of respondents using AI in accounting tools reported positive ROI, and 39% named faster close and reconciliation as a benefit.


Month-end close automation is often where you see those improvements first, because the close narrows to three exception types:


- Payouts that don’t tie to the bank deposit
- Products that aren’t mapped to a QuickBooks item
- Fees missing from a payout


## **Choosing the right accounting automation tool to integrate Shopify with QuickBooks**


An accounting automation tool that integrates Shopify with QuickBooks should handle seven jobs:


- **Payout reconciliation** that matches Shopify’s deposits to actual bank amounts automatically
- **Multi-channel and payment processor sync** to consolidate data from Shopify Payments and third-party gateways, like PayPal or Stripe, plus other sales platforms like Amazon or eBay, if needed
- **Automated fee categorization** for transaction fees, payment processing costs, and platform charges
- **Sales tax breakdown** by jurisdiction to ensure accurate reporting and compliance
- **Inventory and COGS tracking** to update stock levels and calculate cost of goods sold as products move
- **Flexible sync modes** (per-transaction or summary) based on your transaction volume
- **Historical data import** to bring past transactions into QuickBooks without manual backfill


### **Integration options for managing COGS between Shopify and QuickBooks**


Synder, MyWorks, Connex, and the Intuit connector can post cost of goods sold (COGS) to QuickBooks once product unit costs and matching inventory items are in place, while Zapier needs custom Zap steps. In the same demo calls with 412 retail merchants, 44.7% named tracking inventory and COGS as an accounting challenge, second only to manual data entry.


In these four tools, the flow follows the same path: Shopify SKU, then unit cost, then a credit to the inventory asset account and a debit to the COGS account. The difference lies in where the unit cost comes from and which plan includes it.


**Tool** **How COGS reaches QuickBooks** **Plan that includes it**


Synder Per Transaction updates QuickBooks inventory items as they sell; Summary Sync calculates COGS from an imported costs file Essential plan and up


MyWorks Syncs product cost and inventory to QuickBooks items Free plan syncs cost; two-way inventory from Grow


Intuit connector Matches Shopify products to existing QuickBooks items and keeps quantities and costs in sync Free; inventory items need QuickBooks Online Plus or Advanced


Connex Inventory sync with COGS tracking listed on its Shopify app Plan level not published


Zapier No built-in COGS logic; requires custom Zap steps Not included


Your inventory valuation method decides how unit cost is calculated: QuickBooks Online uses FIFO, while QuickBooks Desktop uses weighted average cost unless Enterprise Advanced Inventory is turned on. Pick the method first, then confirm the integration posts at the item level the method needs.


#### **Landed costs, bundles, and purchase orders in COGS**


Shopify inventory tracking holds quantities, but it doesn’t add freight or duties to unit cost. Those costs have to be part of the item cost before any integration can post an accurate COGS figure.


If you include them, set up the landed cost calculation in an inventory system or in QuickBooks, because the integrations above use the unit cost they are given.


Bundles need component-level inventory tracking. In QuickBooks Desktop Premier and Enterprise, a QuickBooks inventory assembly item deducts a bundle’s components when it sells. Check how your integration maps bundle SKUs before you turn on inventory sync.


For stock received against supplier orders, purchase order matching ties the receipt to the bill in QuickBooks. MyWorks syncs purchase orders from Shopify’s Stocky app on its higher plans, and Connex lists purchase order support on its Shopify listing.


### **Match the tool to your business model**


Five questions match a Shopify business to the right QuickBooks integration. Answer them in order:


1. **Who manages your books, you or an accountant? I** f an accountant or bookkeeper manages several clients, look for multi-client access and per-client rules, covered in the accounting firm section below.
2. **Do you need per-order detail or end-of-day summaries?** High-volume stores usually do better with summary syncs that group activity by payout and keep QuickBooks cleaner. Use per-transaction sync if you track inventory or customer- or product-level profitability, since you’ll need individual order details for accurate reporting.
3. **How much inventory and COGS detail do you need?** If gross margin by product matters, choose a tool and plan from the COGS table above.
4. **Are you on QuickBooks Online or QuickBooks Desktop?** Synder, MyWorks, and Connex support both; the Intuit connector and Zapier connect to QuickBooks Online only.
5. **What will an order cost at 2 to 3 times today’s volume, across the channels you plan to add?** If your business spans Shopify, marketplaces like Amazon or eBay, and several payment gateways, look for a tool that pulls everything into QuickBooks. As order volume increases or you add new storefronts, warehouses, or product lines, you’ll need a tool that can grow with you. Choose one that maintains speed, stays stable with higher transaction loads, and won’t require re-mapping your setup every time the business expands.


**Takeaway:** The best tool is the one that keeps your data accurate and aligns with your business processes – choose the sync approach that supports both your current workflow and where the business is headed.


Now that we know what to look for, let’s examine the best options available.


## ****What are the top Shopify QuickBooks integration tools?****


The top Shopify QuickBooks integration tools in 2026 are Synder, MyWorks, the Intuit QuickBooks Online Connector, Connex, and Zapier, and they fit different setups:


- **Synder:** multi-channel sellers that need 30+ sales and payment platforms synced to one QuickBooks file and verified with Auto Reconciliation
- **MyWorks:** QuickBooks Desktop users
- **Intuit connector:** single-store sellers on QuickBooks Online, at no extra cost
- **Connex:** rules-heavy multichannel and wholesale workflows
- **Zapier:** custom multi-app automations


Accounting automation tools for Shopify QuickBooks integration take different approaches to syncing your store data with your accounting software. The main differences lie in how they handle transaction data, what features they offer, and how they’re priced.


### **Shopify accounting services: QuickBooks integration comparison at a glance**


Synder starts at $52/month, MyWorks and Zapier have free plans, the Intuit connector is free with QuickBooks Online, and Connex starts at $4,788/year. The table adds fit, sync method, entry-plan volume, and Shopify App Store rating for the five tools as of October 2026.

### **1. Synder: best for multi-channel sellers**


[Synder](https://synder.com/integrations/quickbooks/shopify/) **** is an accounting automation platform that syncs sales, fees, refunds, and taxes from Shopify, Amazon, PayPal, Stripe, and 30+ other platforms into QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Intuit Enterprise Suite, and Puzzle. Beyond syncing, Synder verifies that data, so payouts tie out to their bank deposits before month-end close.


Because sync and verification happen in one platform, you don’t need a second tool or a spreadsheet to check what was posted. For multi-channel brand[RadRoller](https://synder.com/success-stories/rad/) , that combination saved 40+ hours a month and $2,000+ in bookkeeper costs.


**Core features**


- **Multi-channel sync** connects Shopify, Amazon, eBay, Etsy, PayPal, Stripe, Square, and[30+](https://synder.com/integrations/) other platforms to your accounting software, syncing sales, refunds, fees, and taxes automatically.
- **Per Transaction and Summary Sync modes** let you choose between detailed order-level data or aggregated journal entries based on transaction volume and reporting needs.
- [Smart Rules](https://synder.com/blog/smart-rules/) automate categorization, applying classes, locations, tax codes, and account mappings based on product type, customer data, or transaction details.
- [Auto Reconciliation](https://synder.com/product/auto-reconciliation/) checks synced data against the source platform’s own records, on every plan. Transaction Reconciliation matches every line in your clearing account to the platform’s own records, automated via API, standard upload, or custom mapping, and flags anything that doesn’t tie 100%, so you review only the transactions that need attention. For Summary Sync, Balance Reconciliation verifies that the period matches the platform’s reported starting and ending balances before you post summaries to your books, and every reconciliation keeps a full audit trail you can download or revisit. Payout matching then breaks Shopify payouts into its charges, fees, refunds, and chargebacks, so the deposit ties out to the bank line.
- **Historical data import** brings in past transactions from your sales platforms, so your books are complete from day one without manual backfill.
- **Inventory and COGS tracking** automatically updates stock levels and calculates cost of goods sold as products sell, keeping your balance sheet and profit margins accurate.
- **Open invoice sync** posts Shopify orders with payment terms to QuickBooks as open invoices until they’re paid, on the Essential plan and up.


**Pricing**

Essential From $103/month Up to 3,000 sales transactions/month (1,000 included in the base price), unlimited integrations, hourly sync, COGS tracking

Monthly billing costs about 20% more: Basic is $65/month and Essential starts at $129/month, per[Synder’s pricing page](https://synder.com/pricing/) .


**Suitable for**


Synder is ideal for multi-channel ecommerce businesses selling on Shopify, Amazon, eBay, Etsy, or other platforms, especially if you process hundreds of transactions monthly and need automated categorization. Accounting firms managing multiple clients also benefit from the multi-entity support and customizable rules.


### **2. MyWorks: best for QuickBooks Desktop users**


MyWorks provides flexible Shopify QuickBooks integration supporting both QuickBooks Online and QuickBooks Desktop. The platform offers customizable sync settings with bidirectional inventory management, making it one of the few solutions that properly supports legacy QuickBooks Desktop installations while maintaining modern automation features.


**Core features**


- **Flexible sync options** let you create either invoices or sales receipts in QuickBooks based on your accounting workflow, with the ability to sync orders individually or in summary format.
- **Inventory management** automatically updates stock levels between Shopify and QuickBooks, preventing overselling and reducing manual inventory adjustments; supports multi-location inventory tracking.
- **Order-level detail** includes full customer information, product details, taxes, shipping costs, and payment methods for each transaction.


***Note*** **:** MyWorks comes as two Shopify apps, one for QuickBooks Online and one for QuickBooks Desktop Pro, Premier, and Enterprise. The Desktop app needs the Intuit Web Connector on the computer that hosts the company file, so Desktop updates arrive on a set schedule.


**Pricing**


**Plan** **Price** **What’s included**


Launch $0 (Free Forever) Up to 20 orders/month, sync products, inventory, price, and cost, hourly sync, historical data


Rise $24/month Up to 100 orders/month, 30-minute sync, free setup call


Grow $49/month Up to 300 orders/month, individual or summary sync, two-way inventory, Shopify payouts and refunds


Scale $89/month Up to 1,000 orders/month, purchase orders from Stocky, Shopify Plus B2B features

These prices apply to the QuickBooks Online app, which offers about 20% off with yearly billing, per its[Shopify App Store listing](https://apps.shopify.com/quickbooks-sync-by-myworks) . The[Desktop app](https://apps.shopify.com/quickbooks-desktop-sync) is priced separately:


- Free: up to 50 orders
- Rise, $79/month: up to 100 orders/month
- Grow, $99/month: up to 300 orders/month
- Scale, $129/month: up to 500 orders/month


**Suitable for**


MyWorks suits businesses using QuickBooks Desktop who need modern automation without migrating to QuickBooks Online. The platform suits stores that need detailed order-level data in their books, including full customer profiles and itemized transactions. Multi-location businesses benefit from the inventory tracking features that maintain accurate stock counts across warehouses and retail locations.


### **3. Intuit QuickBooks Online Connector (native Shopify app): best for free single-store setups**


The official Shopify QuickBooks integration from Intuit syncs sales, customer, and product data directly from your Shopify store to QuickBooks Online at no additional cost. Intuit moved merchants to a rebuilt version of the connector in early 2026, which imports individual sales for review and groups sales, refunds, and fees into payout deposits.


**Core features**


- **Payout-based deposits** record confirmed sales as sales receipts plus fee expenses in Undeposited Funds, then group them into one deposit per payout that you match to the bank line, according to[Intuit’s setup guide](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/learn-support/en-us/help-article/manage-integrations/connect-shopify-quickbooks-online/L1Xv7ZCFB_US_en_US) .
- **B2B invoices** import Shopify B2B orders as invoices with the company, payment terms, and PO number, link later payments to them, and send paid status from QuickBooks to Shopify.
- **Product and customer tracking** matches Shopify products to existing QuickBooks items by SKU and name; unmatched products have to be created manually.
- **Sales tax handling** records merchant-collected tax on the sales receipt and books Shop app marketplace tax to Sales Tax Payable.
- **Review queue** holds imported transactions in a For Review tab unless automatic adding is on, and imports up to 12 months of history.


**Pricing**


Free (included with QuickBooks Online subscription)


**Suitable for**


The native connector fits single-store sellers on QuickBooks Online who sell only through Shopify and are comfortable reviewing transactions inside QuickBooks. This tool covers the essentials if you’re just starting out and want basic order syncing without additional costs.


### **4. Connex: best for rules-heavy multichannel and wholesale workflows**


Connex focuses on high-volume, multi-channel businesses that need advanced rule-based automation and custom field mapping. The platform supports Shopify, Amazon, eBay, Walmart, and other platforms with customizable data flows to QuickBooks or Sage Intacct.


**Core features**


- **Advanced rule-based syncing** applies custom logic to categorize transactions by product type, customer data, or order value without manual intervention.
- **Multi-channel support** connects Shopify, Amazon, eBay, Walmart, and other platforms to QuickBooks, consolidating all sales data in one place.
- **Error handling** detects sync failures automatically and provides troubleshooting steps, reducing the time spent fixing broken integrations.


**Pricing**


**Plan** **Price** **What’s included**

Platinum $5,988 a year (499/month) Up to 36,000 orders/year, three sales channels, deposit matching, reports refreshed every 6 hours


Enterprise Custom pricing 36,000+ orders/year, four or more sales channels, custom workflows and reporting


Connex bills its plans annually and charges 10 cents per order over the plan limit, according to[Connex’s pricing page](https://connexecommerce.com/features-and-pricing) . Guided implementation costs $900 on top of the subscription, and new subscriptions are fully refundable within the first 30 days.


**Suitable for**


Connex is suitable for businesses with complex accounting requirements, multiple sales channels, or unique categorization needs. If you’re managing wholesale and retail operations, selling internationally, or need advanced rule-based automation, Connex provides the flexibility to handle it.


### **5. Zapier: best for custom multi-app workflows**


Zapier connects Shopify to QuickBooks through custom automation workflows (called “Zaps”) that trigger actions based on specific events. Unlike dedicated integrations, Zapier provides a flexible, template-based approach where you build your own data flows between the two platforms.


**Core features**


- **Custom workflow builder** lets you create automations with triggers (like “New Shopify Order”) and actions (like “Create QuickBooks Invoice”) without coding.
- **Pre-built templates** provide ready-made workflows for common tasks like creating invoices, adding customers, or syncing products between Shopify and QuickBooks.
- **Multi-step Zaps** allow complex workflows with conditional logic, filters, and multiple actions triggered by a single event.
- **Multiple app integrations** enable you to connect Shopify and QuickBooks with other business tools in the same workflow, creating end-to-end automation.


**Pricing**


**Plan** **Price** **What’s included**


Free $0 100 tasks/month, two-step Zaps, 1 user, 15-minute update intervals


Professional From $19.99/month Multi-step Zaps, unlimited Premium apps, webhooks, 1 user, 2-minute updates


Team From $69/month Shared Zaps and folders, shared app connections, SAML SSO, up to 25 users, 1-minute updates


Enterprise Custom pricing Custom annual task limits, unlimited users, advanced admin permissions, Technical Account Manager


Paid plans scale from 100 to 2 million tasks a month, and yearly billing saves 33%, according to[Zapier’s pricing page](https://zapier.com/pricing) . If an account goes over its plan’s task limit, Zapier switches to pay-per-task billing at a higher rate unless you turn that option off.


**Suitable for**


Zapier works best for businesses that need custom automation beyond standard integrations or want to connect Shopify and QuickBooks with other tools in multi-step workflows. If you’re comfortable building your own data flows and need flexibility rather than plug-and-play simplicity, Zapier provides the customization options. However, it’s not ideal for high-volume stores or businesses needing dedicated payout reconciliation features.


### **Shopify QuickBooks integration support by QuickBooks edition**

- Payroll tax updates

Synder covers all five elements for Shopify and for any additional sales or payment platform connected to the same QuickBooks file, and its Auto Reconciliation checks that payouts tie to their deposits. The per-order sync vs summary sync choice decides how many transactions post to QuickBooks each day. A store with 200 orders a day posts 200 sales receipts in per-order mode and one journal entry per processor in summary mode.

#### **What to do before the first sync**


Every Shopify QuickBooks integration needs account mapping before the first sync, so sales, tax, fee, refund, and clearing lines have destination accounts in QuickBooks. A clean QuickBooks Chart of Accounts, with separate accounts for each processor’s fees and clearing balance, is what makes the reports in the automation section possible.


Testing a small batch first also confirms fees and refunds post to the right accounts. For Shopify Payments specifically, compare the first synced week against the Shopify Payments settlement report before you turn on automatic posting.
